patches.value: Fix arbitrary r>0, let J=[r/2,3r/2], choose compact C from H003, and define C*=C∪{0}. The set C* is compact and nonempty; outside C* we still have u=q throughout J. The function (x,τ)↦|e_t(x,τ)| is continuous on C*×J by smoothness, and C*×J is compact by M005. Apply M019; its bounded-above conclusion supplies a real upper bound, so choose a finite K≥0 with |e_t(x,τ)|≤K for all (x,τ)∈C*×J. Define b(x)=K·1_{C*}(x). Outside C*, e_t=0 by smoothness and constancy of u on the open spatial complement; hence |e_t(x,τ)|≤b(x) for every x and τ∈J. By N001 every compact set is measurable and has finite Lebesgue measure. M008 makes the constant K integrable on C*, and M009 makes b integrable on ℝⁿ. Define F(τ)(x)=e(x,τ) and Fprime(τ)(x)=e_t(x,τ). Smoothness implies strong measurability; N001 gives F(r) integrable and Fprime(r) strongly measurable. The interval (r/2,3r/2) is a neighborhood of r. The pointwise parameter derivative of F is Fprime by smoothness, and the bound by b holds for every x and every τ in this neighborhood. Thus M006 applies and yields differentiability of E at r with E′(r)=∫e_t(x,r)dx. Since r was arbitrary, the output follows.
